author: rishi_suri
text: #AbhijeetDipke’s June 6 Protest: The #CockroachJantaParty Moves Offline @abhijeet_dipke’s call for supporters to gather on June 6 and demand the resignation of Education Minister @dpradhanbjp marks an important moment in the evolution of the so-called “Cockroach Janta Party” movement. For the first time, a phenomenon that has largely existed online is attempting to test its strength on the streets. The issues being raised by Dipke and his followers may well be genuine. Concerns about examinations, recruitment processes, transparency and accountability in public institutions resonate with many young Indians. Governments should never dismiss such grievances out of hand. However, serious questions remain about the movement itself. The extraordinary growth of the Cockroach Janta Party across social media platforms was anything but ordinary. Its follower counts exploded in a manner that appeared highly unusual and, to many observers, distinctly inorganic. Large numbers of bot-like accounts, coordinated amplification patterns and suspicious engagement metrics across platforms have led to persistent doubts about how much of the movement’s apparent popularity reflects real people rather than digital manipulation. That does not automatically invalidate every concern raised by its supporters. But it does raise legitimate questions about who is driving the movement, how it achieved such rapid visibility, and whether its online strength accurately reflects real-world public support. The June 6 protest will therefore be closely watched. Not only will it provide a clearer picture of the movement’s genuine grassroots reach, it will also test whether an online phenomenon can successfully transition into an organised offline force. Recent developments in several countries across South Asia have demonstrated how digitally mobilised protest movements can quickly escalate beyond their original demands and, in some cases, turn confrontational or violent. For that reason alone, any government would be expected to monitor such gatherings carefully. The challenge for authorities will be maintaining public order without overreacting. Excessive force or heavy-handed action risks elevating fringe figures into national symbols. At the same time, legitimate concerns about the origins, methods and objectives of the movement cannot simply be ignored. June 6 may ultimately reveal whether the Cockroach Janta Party is a genuine mass movement, a social media mirage, or something in between. @CJP_2029 @Cockroachisback

text: Something doesn't add up. The Cockroach Janta Party was launched around a specific grievance involving the CJI and the Education Minister. Yet, within weeks, its Chief Spokesperson is talking about entirely different issues: • Culture of non-answerability • Not holding press conferences • Not talking to the media • Suppression of independent voices If these are now the central themes, then this movement appears to have evolved far beyond its original stated purpose. That is precisely what concerns me. A protest that begins with one issue but quickly shifts into a broader political narrative naturally raises questions about its real objectives. Citizens have every right to protest, but they also have every right to ask: What is the actual agenda here? The sudden transition from a specific grievance to a full-scale critique of governance deserves scrutiny, not blind applause.

text: Not taking prior permission for the Jantar Mantar protest is not an oversight. It is the plan. They want Delhi Police to intervene. They want visuals. Even a court is a designated space for justice and you still file a proper petition, follow procedure, and respect the process. A hospital is designated for treatment and you still register before the doctor sees you. Designation means the right is recognised. It does not mean rules disappear. Permission is not suppression. It is order. And those who resist even that basic step are not protecting your right to protest. They are protecting their right to chaos. Who exactly are these “angry youths” they keep invoking? Anger is real. Manipulation of that anger is a political industry. Dissent has a constitutional home. It is called the Supreme Court. Use it. But understand this clearly, the ones calling you to the streets will not share your FIR or your ruined career. They will share your photograph.

text: My two cents on what's going to happen in Delhi on Saturday, June 6, 2026. @abhijeet_dipke, the founder of the @Cockroachisback, has announced to land in Delhi at 0800 Hrs that day. It is unlikely that the Modi govt will try to arrest him there, knowing the massive support the CJP is receiving from all sections of society. I'm not expecting a crowd of thousands to reach the airport to receive him. If they do make it there, the Modi govt will try to scatter them under the pretext of airport security issues. NO FORCE WILL BE USED & NO ARRESTS WILL BE MADE AT THE AIRPORT itself, given the heavy presence of foreign visitors and the world's eyes on this protest. As per the announced plans, the CJP will then head to the Parliament Street PS to seek permission for a protest later that day at Jantar Mantar. Though JM is a designated space for protests and the police should grant permission, knowing Amit Shah well, the Delhi police will likely deny it, citing law & order issues and protocol rules for applying. This is where story will unfold. The moment this news breaks, the protestors who have started arriving to join the protest, especially the angry students & Gen-Z masses, might sit in protest anyway. This will trigger a clash between the police and the protestors. The govt might use force against them. This is where they might arrest Abhijeet Dipke under the pretext of inciting the crowd to disrupt law & order and creating unrest in the country. The BJP’s pre-prepared toolkit will be launched to defame the CJP as a foreign-funded entity formed to create civil unrest in India. If the CJP decides to postpone the protest due to the lack of permission, the Modi govt, together with its 'godi media' & IT cell, will start calling it a failed protest and label Dipke and others 'Darpok'. It is unlikely that the protest will be allowed to take place smoothly. Instead, there are chances that the govt may take another route by offering to hold a dialogue and giving false assurances, just as they did during the farmers' and the Ladakh protest. It will be interesting to see on what charges and at what stage they will arrest Abhijeet Dipke to weaken the party and the movement. However, this time it is not just Muslims, farmers, defense personnel, or bankers; it is a charged-up Gen-Z. THINGS ARE DEFINITELY NOT GOING TO BE EASY FOR MODI FROM NOW ON. So, I suggest everyone joining the protest remain calm and not lose their temper. THE WORLD IS WATCHING. Let them use force if they do; it will only strengthen the storm against this autocratic, shameless govt. To everyone else, whether you are a student, Gen-Z, or a parent; Hindu or Muslim; rich or poor; upper or lower caste; irrespective of your skin color, what you eat, what you wear, or what language you speak, HIT THE ROADS AND JOIN THE MOVEMENT. There can't be a better way to show a common man's strength to this autocratic, shameless, and failed govt than by protesting and joining a similar non-cooperative movement. author: sanjraj
text: 'Deep State' Dipke's Cockroach Protest Stands Exposed; Leftist Roaches Crawl Over Jantar Mantar Roaches roasting under Delhi’s baking sun were roaring one line today — "Cockroaches never fear, never die." That part is true. But there’s something else about cockroaches they’re not telling you. Did you know a cockroach can survive without its head? Cut the head off, and it keeps walking for days — on pure instinct. It can’t eat. It can’t think. It just… keeps moving until it starves or rots from the inside. That is exactly what we are watching today. June 6, 2026. Jantar Mantar — that sacred feeding ground where India’s professional protestors have dined for decades. The Cockroach Janata Party had promised a mega youth revolution. NEET leaks. Exam scams. Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation. Twenty-two million algorithm-engineered bots screaming fire across Instagram and X. The Roach in Chief himself — Abhijeet Dipke — landed fresh off a flight from Boston, constitution in one hand, promises of flowers for the police in the other. They said the streets would burn. They said Gen-Z would rise. What actually showed up? A few hundred cockroaches at best. Not even two thousand. Outnumbered by Delhi Police and the bored media crew waiting for a spectacle that never arrived. The same old headless wonders – Samajwadi remnants, RJD ruffians, Congress leftovers, AAPtards, and the usual left radicals – are twitching their antennae, desperately sniffing for any scent of chaos. These political cockroaches had their heads severed in 2014. Electoral heads. Power heads. The constitutional route to power was shut for them — not by any conspiracy, but by the repeated verdict of the Indian people. More than a decade out of power with zero realistic hope of returning through the ballot box. So what do they do? They keep twitching. They keep marching. They try to reattach their severed heads by plugging into fresh student anger — NEET leaks, exam scams, anything that hurts young people — and then coating that genuine grievance with the same old anarchist poison. This is not new. This is the exact same script we saw in anti-CAA. The exact same script we saw in the farmers’ protest. Manufacture outrage, import professional andolanjeevis from SFI, AISA, and AISF, bring in the Dafli Gang to beat Umar Khalid-style rhythms, and then pray that the resulting chaos becomes so big that the constitutional order cracks. If you cannot win elections, trigger enough street fire that you can usurp power through the back door — exactly as their foreign masters and deep-state scriptwriters have taught them for years. That is why Abhijeet Dipke flies in from Boston. That is why the same discredited AAPiyas suddenly discover “student outrage". That is why Sauraav Das, their spokesperson, lasts ten minutes in the Delhi sun before retreating under a tree with cold coffee in his hand – while still demanding the prime minister's resignation. These are not revolutionaries. These are parasites who cannot stand the heat of real sunlight or real accountability. They keep saying, “We are not a planned party. This is pure students’ outrage.” But the moment the Dafli starts and the old slogans return, the mask slips. The same people who spent ten years crying only about Hindu-Muslim politics are now trying to turn every exam paper leak into a constitutional crisis. The hypocrisy is not even clever anymore. It is just pathetic. And the youth? The real Gen-Z and millennials? They stayed home. Because twenty-two million followers were mostly bots. Because the people leading this circus have been discredited so many times that even teenagers can smell the rot. The real students of this country are busy preparing for the next exam, building their futures, and watching India rise — not waiting to be extras in someone else’s failed revolution. Real accountability on NEET and exam leaks is necessary. Absolutely. But turning every grievance into another prolonged dharna to topple a democratically elected government? The people have seen this movie too many times. They are not buying tickets anymore. The cockroaches will keep bumbling. They will survive the head cut for a few more days — maybe weeks. They will keep twitching on pure instinct, hoping the next manufactured outrage finally gives them the chaos they need. But without real public backing, without electoral legitimacy, without a head – starvation is inevitable. Infection has already begun. This civilisational nation is not going to let a handful of scurrying roaches feast on manufactured outrage and turn it into unconstitutional anarchy. History has it: India does not rise on wishful anarchy. It never will. The headless march has already begun to die. We are just watching the slow, inevitable end. author: vipinsarohayt
text: History bears witness to the fact that those in power dread nothing more than individuals who ask questions without waving a political flag. Today, the very youth who ask these uncomfortable questions have taken to the streets. Gathered at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar, these young minds are contemptuously being labeled as "TILCHATTE" by some, who are even callously talking about spraying HIT on them. While the BJP’s frustration is understandable, why the hell are these Congressmen losing their minds and overstepping their bounds? The very youth you are abusing have held up a mirror today to the ruling party, the opposition, and the media alike. * **No political stage,** * **No constellation of big-shot leaders,** * **No electoral rallies,** * **No crowds herded into hired buses.** Yet, thousands of youngsters stood their ground. Most of them were likely sitting on a scorching road, under a blazing sun, without fans or tents, enduring conditions like a furnace for the very first time in their lives. Those who are undermining them or mocking them are not just insulting these protestors, they are mocking the entire Gen Z and the younger generation of this nation. These are the very youth who have been raising their voices for years against **unemployment, paper leaks, recruitment scams, inflation, and a compromised media**. Yet, in response, they are mockingly branded as "TILCHATTE." If this youth quietly tolerates everything, they are hailed as the "future of the nation," but the moment they demand accountability, they are reduced to pests. When Sonam Wangchuk arrived at the venue, people immediately began painting him as the "New Anna Hazare." Such comparisons are merely a testament to their desperation. Even the Congress is mocking Sonam Wangchuk. They evidently have no respect even for those whom the Modi government jailed simply for speaking up for the betterment of this country. Some are dismissing this gathering of young citizens as a mere "bubble," claiming that barely 100 to 200 people showed up. To those skeptics, let me say this: deny it all you want, but you cannot escape the reality that this is the boiling wrath of the youth. The anger was always there. Today, it simply erupted and found expression. Even if it is a passing bubble, the youth desperately need a platform. Their rage and resistance should not be measured by mere headcount, but understood through the depth of their anguish. The voice that echoed at Jantar Mantar today is not just a protest; it is the restlessness of a generation that no longer wants rhetoric, it demands answers. Dismissing lakhs of young citizens of this country as "cockroaches" will not make the problems vanish. However, it *will* definitively prove that the establishment has absolutely no answers to their questions. **Keep questioning.** **Keep demanding answers.** Because in a true democracy, a citizen’s greatest weapon will always be their voice.

author: clashreport
text: Thousands of students descended on New Delhi's Jantar Mantar under the banner of the "Cockroach Janta Party", a satirical youth movement that reclaimed a term India's Chief Justice reportedly used to dismiss unemployed young people, and turned it into a rallying cry against the country's broken exam system. The movement, founded by 30-year-old Abhijeet Dipke, has amassed 22 million Instagram followers and 800,000 signatures demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. The immediate trigger: the NEET-UG 2026 medical entrance exam paper leak, affecting over 10 million students. Protesters wore cockroach masks and carried placards reading "Cockroaches do not die."

author: augadhbhudeva
text: Latest Guardian Sob Story On Umar Khalid Is Another Indication That NEET Is Just A Mask On 30th June, The Guardian published a sympathetic profile of Umar Khalid, presenting the accused in the larger conspiracy case related to the 2020 anti-Hindu Delhi Riots as one of India’s most prominent “political prisoners” and a victim of a government crackdown on dissent. Built around reflections on prison, fading hope, Dostoevsky and Bhagat Singh, the article largely avoided examining the prosecution’s case against him. The article needs to be scrutinised not just for what it said, but also for what it deliberately left outside the frame. The publication came amid open support for Khalid from the leadership and supporters of the so-called Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), whose protests were launched around the NEET paper leak and youth issues. However, protesters and CJP supporters, both online and offline, have called for Umar Khalid to be freed. Titled “‘Humanity is a privilege’: Umar Khalid on his six years in an Indian jail without trial”, The Guardian article was written by Hannah Ellis-Petersen, the publication’s Delhi correspondent who is known for her anti-India propaganda. In the article, she described Khalid as an activist, a left-wing rights campaigner and a fierce critic of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. She claimed that he had become a symbol of the alleged weaponisation of the judicial system against government opponents.

author: augadhbhudeva
text: In a recent interview with Samdish Bhatia on Unfiltered by Samdish, Dipke claimed that he had kept his movement peaceful, Constitution-centric and difficult to discredit. Out of no where, Samdish remarked that his surname was not Khalid, to which Dipke said that had he been a Khalid, Saifi or Muslim, he would have been in jail. Through the remark, Dipke appeared to suggest that so-called Muslim “activists” such as Umar Khalid were imprisoned because of their religious identity, conveniently ignoring the serious criminal and conspiracy charges against them. The forceful insertion of Khalid’s reference was uncanny but gave the idea what exactly they were trying to do. Spokesperson Saurav Das went further, describing the charges against Khalid as “false” and “frivolous” and calling his imprisonment a blot on India’s judiciary. Another CJP spokesperson, Vijeta Dahiya, attempted to reduce the case against Khalid to a speech quoting Mahatma Gandhi and his presence in a WhatsApp group. When questioned about the larger conspiracy case and the more than 50 people killed during the Delhi Riots, Dahiya fell back on the argument that no trial had taken place and accused the journalist questioning him of being “godi media”.

author: augadhbhudeva
text: The argument was framed as a defence of due process. Let the trial happen, punish him if he is guilty and release him if he is innocent. However, the same people repeatedly cited the absence of a conviction as proof that the charges were false. They simultaneously demanded that the court process be allowed to conclude and treated the fact that it had not concluded as a declaration of innocence. The procedural history was also more complicated than the slogan “six years without trial” suggested. Khalid’s latest plea, which was submitted to the court on 6th June, the same day CJP launched its first protest in Delhi, identified itself as his third bail application. His first and second bail applications were dismissed, as were subsequent appeals before the Delhi High Court. His Special Leave Petition was dismissed by the Supreme Court in January 2026, followed by the dismissal of his review petition in April. The application itself reproduced the Supreme Court’s observation that the case involved several accused persons, voluminous documentary and electronic evidence and accusations concerning a structured and continuing conspiracy. The court also said the record did not show that Umar Khalid and the other accused were in jail only because of prosecution delays or that they had played no role in causing those delays. While a debate over prolonged pre-trial detention is legitimate in a broader context, in Umar Khalid’s case, the delay in the trial was not caused by the justice system but by the accused themselves. Umar Khalid and the other accused in the larger conspiracy case used every possible tactic to delay the trial and then used the delay as an excuse to seek bail. From repeated bail pleas to pleas seeking to prevent the trial from starting, there was enough evidence to show that India’s justice system was not the culprit behind the six-year-long delay in the trial. CJP Protestors Called Umar Khalid Their Leader Support for Khalid was also visible at CJP’s first major protest at Jantar Mantar on 6th June. One protester was filmed declaring, “Umar Khalid is our leader.” Another said that he supported Khalid and saw nothing wrong with doing so. A CJP supporter also described Khalid and Sharjeel Imam as potential future occupants of the country’s highest political offices.

text: The lukewarm response that the Cockroach Janta Party founders are witnessing at Jantar Mantar are the signs of the times we live in. Maasive following on Insta and Fb does not translate into on ground support. The generation which follows you on social media, especially the one's born post 2000, will not be willing to hit the streets. Heck, they are not even willing to walk down the road to get their daily household needs, because Blinkit, Zomato, Swiggy and their fourth friend Amazon, are all there, at their service. If only Urban Company and Pronto had an option, where one could hire protestors on one's behalf to protest for a cause, then the dwindling prospects of Cockroach Janta Party would have got a massive boost, but as of now, that functionality is not provided, but you never know. Second, the faces of this movement lack charisma and public connect. Abhijeet Dipke is no mass leader, like Arvind Kejriwal, his persona and his background does not make the person behind the screen go like 'Woah, he is the guy I am willing to take 1 day off from my office'. Saurav Das and the other fellow, who keeps dancing to songs of 1990's Bollywood are not even Twitter celebrities. Also why would the generation following them, born post 2000, vibe to songs of Bollywood movies of 90's and the era of 2000 to 2010. I did enjoy their dance performance, but then I am not your target audience. Similarly for all of Sonam Wangchuk's achievements, he too is no Anna Hazare and India of 2026, is not India of 2012. Life in India has become more comfortable, while the income disparity remains, both these truths run parallel. The issue of NEET, Ethanol are the one's which the ruling government should be rightly questioned about and one can even see supporters of the current government taking them to task on these 2 major issues. However, the fast unto death emotional blackmail type of protest is passe. It no longer appeals to the current generation, neither to the one's previous to them, who actually grew up watching such protests overturn governments of the day. A few days back, came across a clip of my friend @Iyervval where he spoke about how we don't realize that how far India has come from the days of abject poverty and this is where the answer to the lack of response to CJP's Dharna Party lies. author: md_deepesh
text: I want to take a moment to thank Abhijeet Dipke. For 19 days now, he has been teaching this nation a masterclass. Not in exam reform. In something more valuable. He flew in from Boston. Unemployed. To save India's students. Then handed the mic to Allah. Kashmir. RSS. Umar Khalid. Wait. Where is Dharmendra Pradhan? Well. He is not generating any TRP. And he is having fun continuing as Education Minister. Turns out the fastest way to save a minister's job is to hire professional protestors. Pradhan should be sending flowers to Jantar Mantar. Maybe Pradhan hired Abhijeet Dipke. Nobody even remembers his name is on the placards anymore. Special mention to Sonam Wangchuk. Came for a guest appearance. Stayed to become the whole show. 19 days without food. Visibly. While everyone else on that stage eats on schedule. And the menu is incredible. Continental on Monday. Chinese on Tuesday. Hyderabadi on Wednesday. American on Thursday. Repeat. With desserts. Tea. Coffee. Imagine fasting for 19 days next to a buffet you're not invited to. Every speaker walks up. Says a few lines about Allah. Ambedkar. Kashmir. RSS. Umar Khalid. Then walks off to eat. Wangchuk stays. Hungry. Foolish. Watching. Wondering if anyone even remembers what this started as. At some point even the most patient man starts doing math. If Wangchuk could speak freely right now. Off the record. We suspect it would not be about the education ministry. It would be about catering. Here's the real service Dipke has done this country. He has finally taught us how to spot a cockroach. Not the ones NEET aspirants are competing against for a medical seat. The ones standing on a stage at Jantar Mantar. Holding a mic. Talking about everything except the paper leak that started this. And still don't know who is President of India. The real students are indoors. Revising. Silent. Unheard. The stage belongs to everyone else now. So thank you, Abhijeet Dipke. You didn't get Pradhan to resign. You got India to forget why he should. That takes talent.

text: #WATCH | Delhi | On CJP protest, Congress MP Shashi Tharoor says, "When a non-violent protest is taking place, what is the reason for a lathi-charge? Lathi charge is not an act of non-violence. It is an act of violence. I don't understand the logic of this. Similarly here in Parliament, everyone knows these are burning issues across the country. It would be logical to have a discussion on them. Parliament is supposed to be the place where we can ventilate the voice of the people, the concerns of the people. Once we do that, we all know the government has a majority. As the old saying goes, the Opposition must have its say because the government will have its way. They have the majority. But at least let parliament be a forum where these concerns can be heard, can be truly ventilated and voiced, where various people can represent the views of their constituents. Then the government can disagree. But right now, just refusing a discussion is what has led to today's disruption because the opposition wanted these issues up there, wanted an opportunity to talk about them on the floor of the house. If Parliament is not for raising these issues, then honestly, what is it for? I mean, it can't just be a sort of notice board for the government to announce its bills and get them passed with a rubber stamp. That's not what Parliament is all about. It should be a forum where all these views can be heard, discussed, debated as necessary and then passed. The Prime Minister has sought cooperation from the opposition. We'll cooperate if they cooperate. The idea should be that there should be mutual cooperation. Let them permit certain discussions. This has got to be give and take. text: Heart goes out to NEET Aspirants across India who feel cheated and want transparency and accountability. text: STORY | Union Cabinet approves draft bill for stricter punishments in paper leak cases The Union Cabinet on Friday approved a draft bill to ensure stricter punishments for paper leaks, hours after Prime Minister Narendra Modi made an announcement in this effect, official sources said. The Cabinet meeting chaired by the prime minister at the Parliament House complex approved the draft bill to hand stricter punishments to those involved in paper leaks than the existing laws, the sources said. The regime's message was clear: stay in your rooms. Stay out of the streets. Stay silent. But the students of DU had a different message. As a Response...they gathered at the Arts Faculty. Not in thousands but in spirit. Not with permission but with purpose. They became the voice that the Chancellor, a bootlicker of Modi and the RSS, tried to silence. They carried the pain of NEET aspirants who died by suicide. They carried the memory of students lathi-charged, tear-gassed, and detained. They carried the demand that Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan must resign. And they carried something else: the refusal to be intimidated. The Gen-Z movement has spread beyond Jantar Mantar. It has entered the classrooms, the hostels, the corridors of power. The regime can close 17 metro stations. It can cut the internet. It can deploy 45 battalions. It can issue a thousand advisories. But it cannot stop a generation that has decided: we will not stay away. The Chancellor of DU bent the knee to the regime. The students bent the arc of history. To every student at DU who stood up: you are not alone. You are the voice of a nation that refuses to be silent. And you will not be forgotten.✊🏻🇮🇳

author: sardesairajdeep
text: I first met @AshutoshRanka two months ago, when the NEET paper leak controversy had just erupted, well before the CJP was formed. He had painstakingly compiled data on every major paper leak in India over the last two decades and sent it to me on WhatsApp. The research was meticulous and deeply impressive. Little did I imagine that this same young engineering graduate would soon be sitting across the table from two Union ministers, negotiating on behalf of student protesters. As he told me, he had never even been to Jantar Mantar before this. Ashutosh isn’t a professional agitator. He’s an idealistic young Indian who chose to act. I interviewed him last night after the CJP-government talks. He looked exhausted, seemed unwell, but spoke with remarkable clarity and conviction. If there’s one lesson from the last few weeks, it’s this: never underestimate the power of informed, idealistic youth. text: Jantar Mantar Agitation Withdrawn as Centre Accedes to Key Demands! The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has officially announced the end of its multi-week protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar following the third round of high-level negotiations with a central government delegation comprising Union Ministers J.P. Nadda and Jitendra Singh. Speaking at a joint press conference, CJP National Spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka confirmed that the agitation was called off after the government accepted its core demands, starting with the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. In addition to the minister's exit, the Centre agreed to: - Withdraw all FIRs and legal cases registered against protesting students and organizers, guaranteeing no future retaliatory action. - Provide maximum financial compensation under regulatory provisions to the families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide amid the examination controversy. - Consider the 5-point charter on examination system reforms submitted by the student leaders. - CJP spokespersons urged all student protesters to vacate the venue peacefully and return home as the government pledged to honor its commitments in good faith. #CJPProtest #JantarMantar #DharmendraPradhan #NEET #StudentVictory

author: sauravdassss
text: 🚨STATEMENT We are deeply concerned by multiple reports reaching us of students and other protestors being targeted, detained, or arrested by various state agencies, particularly in Assam, West Bengal, and Bihar. The Cockroach Janta Party had called off its nationwide protest only after the Government of India assured us that no punitive action would be taken against any protestor, either now or in the future, in any BJP-ruled or NDA-ruled states. The reports emerging from these states are therefore a matter of grave concern. First, we wish to assure every protestor that our legal team is already coordinating with brilliant lawyers in the concerned states to secure the release of those detained and to extend all possible legal assistance. This has been happening from Day 1. Second, we call upon the Government of India, particularly @JPNadda ji and @DrJitendraSingh ji, to immediately honour the assurance given to us by ensuring the release of those detained and by directing that no coercive or retaliatory action is taken against any protestor anywhere in the country. The FIRs registered ought to be withdrawn too. The Government of India is also reminded of its commitment to furnish us the written guarantee in this regard by tomorrow, Tuesday, 28 July 2026. author: sauravdassss
text: 🚨URGENT STATEMENT🚨 The interim order passed by the Supreme Court of India in the batch of PILs related to the CJP protest must ring alarm bells across the country. In particular, Direction No. 4, which permits governments to proceed with existing FIRs and carry out investigations, raises extremely serious concerns. This direction stands in direct contradiction to the solemn assurance and guarantee extended by the Government of India to the youth of this nation on 25 July 2026, namely, that the FIRs would be withdrawn and that no protester would be directly or indirectly targeted for participating in the peaceful movement. It was on the strength of that solemn assurance, and in complete good faith, that the Cockroach Janta Party called off its nationwide protest. We now have a credible apprehension that the Government of India and BJP-ruled states may seek to use and weaponise this order of the Bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant to continue FIRs against individual protesters and subject them to great harassment. This was precisely our concern from day one: that courts could be used, directly or indirectly, to achieve political ends by targeting peaceful dissent. Equally troubling is the fact that the interim order was not opposed by the government's lawyers, despite the Central Government being fully aware that talks/assurances with the CJP had continued until as recently as late last night and that a solemn agreement had already been arrived at on 25 July. The court's uninformed order is therefore wholly unacceptable. A solemn public assurance given to thousands of young students and protesters cannot be diluted, undermined, or rendered meaningless through subsequent legal developments, in a surreptitious manner. It only results in breach of public trust. In any event, nothing in the interim order prevents the Government of India or the concerned BJP/NDA ruled State Governments from withdrawing the FIRs or deciding not to proceed against peaceful protesters, like done by Bihar and Assam governments. The power to withdraw or not pursue such cases continues to rest with the executive. The court has not mandated that governments must definitely continue with the FIRs. That would be a deliberate misreading. The Government must not invoke the Court’s order as a justification for reneging on the commitment it made on 25 July. We therefore demand that the Government of India and the concerned BJP/NDA State Governments immediately place the terms of this solemn assurance before the Supreme Court in the pending proceedings so that there is complete transparency regarding the commitments already made to the youth of this country and so that the court can withdraw and make an informed order in the future. The youth of India entered into this understanding in good faith. That good faith must not be betrayed. Institutions of constitutional importance must never be politicised and weaponised to not honour the guarantees. The deadline for the Government of India to honour its guarantees expires today. We once again call upon it to fulfil every commitment it made: withdraw the FIRs, ensure that no protester is subjected to future punitive action, and honour both the letter and the spirit of the assurance that brought an end to the protest. Failing this, and as previously declared, the Cockroach Janta Party will have no option but to resume its nationwide protest to protect the students and young protesters who stood up not for themselves alone, but for the future of this nation. A government that breaks its word cannot expect the youth to remain silent. If the guarantees are dishonoured, the streets of India will once again become the voice of its young.

text: Couldn’t Agree More On This 👍🏾 Arnab Goswami Appeals To Government to Arrest, Book and Not Forgive The Dirty CJP Groups Arnab Goswami issues a direct and powerful call to the government: The officials must swiftly apprehend, charge, and not show leniency towards those concealing themselves behind the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) facade! The real nature of the CJP's 26-day protest at Jantar Mantar has been revealed. By coordinating brutal "goonda tactics" against the Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force members, and causing heaps of waste along with vandalized public property, Arnab reveals how a genuine student concern regarding the NEET-UG matter was entirely taken over. The available evidence indicating a well-coordinated "toolkit" operation, financed by outside forces, designed to instigate Red Fort-style chaos and promote a regime-change agenda in the core of the national capital. Arnab insists on complete responsibility. He urges law enforcement and the government to establish a firm boundary against this foreign-supported street violence and psychological manipulation. Will the actual provocateurs of the Jantar Mantar riots, such as CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, be subjected to the full extent of the law? Can a movement founded on violent rhetoric, harmful slogans, and public destruction be permitted to escape accountability under the label of "student protests"? This is a passionate appeal, the irrefutable proof of the CJP’s devastation, and the crucial national discussion on safeguarding India's democratic institutions from mob brutality.
